title: Play the ace from a hand of five cards held in one gripper, keeping the other four in hand
keywords: taking one sheet out of a held stack
instruction: Play the ace from the hand of cards you are holding: take it out of the hand and lay it face up on the blue cross. Keep the other four cards in your hand.
context: Playing a card from your hand is the basic move of nearly every card game (trick-taking games, rummy, poker draws): one hand holds the cards fanned, the other draws one card out and lays it down, and the rest of the hand stays held. It is selective extraction: taking one thin sheet out of a stack you are gripping yourself without losing the others. A card is 0.29 mm thick and is held only by being pressed between the holding fingers and the card behind it, so a pinch of that card alone cannot pull it out of a firm grip: the holding hand has to relax just enough for that one card to slide, and not so much that the others slip out, then close again.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the robot, y left; heights above the table. Five standard poker-size playing cards (plastic-coated paper, 6.35 x 8.89 x 0.029, 1.55 g each): an ace, a two, a six, a four and a five. They are held in the left gripper as a fan, as laid out on the 1:1 template fan_template.svg: 20 degrees apart, all turned about one point 0.8 in from each card's lower right corner (both edges), faces up; from the fan's left, ace, two, six, four, five, the ace in front and the five at the back. That pivot point is at (26, 8), 15 above the table. The fan's plane rises 30 degrees from level, away from the robot, faces up and toward the robot; the six points straight to the robot's right (-y), so the fan's top edge faces the right arm. The left gripper is closed on the five corners at the pivot, pointing along the six (toward -y), its pad tips 1.9 past the pivot, fingers closing across the fan's plane; left arm joints (rad) -0.232, 1.787, 0.456, 1.329, 1.339, -1.046. The right arm starts in its ready pose with its gripper open. On the table, a blue tape cross of two 4 x 0.5 strips, centred at (33, -17). Nothing else.
scoring: Scored at the end of the trial, from a photo and the trial video. A card is in the hand if it is held between the left gripper's pads and no part of it is lower than 3 cm above the table. The ace lies on the table if no corner of it is more than 0.5 cm up. 0 if any of the other four cards leaves the hand at any time during the trial, or the ace is still in the hand at the end. Otherwise: 0.25 with the ace out of the hand (held, or anywhere off the table); 0.5 with the ace lying on the table, face down, tilted more than 10 degrees from level, or more than 10 cm from the cross's centre; 0.75 with it lying face up and flat (within 10 degrees) with its centre within 10 cm of the cross's centre; 1.0 with it face up and flat within 5 cm of the cross's centre, the right gripper at least 3 cm from it and every card at rest (under 2 cm/s).
reset_notes: Lay the five cards face up on the printed template (five first, ace last), move the left arm to the holding joints with its gripper open, slide the pads over the template's cross along the six's length until their tips are 1.9 cm past it, and close the gripper. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid cards at full size and weight (63.5 x 88.9 x 0.29 mm, 1.55 g, sourced); friction estimated (card on card 0.26, fingertip on card 0.38). The simulated gripper is a stiff position spring with rigid pads, so the left grip is eased by position (0.13 mm a side); a real gripper's softer pads will need a different amount, but the same ease and close. The trial starts with the fan in the left gripper, set at reset before the policy acts. The cross is drawn only. Not tried on a physical rig.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (in the first 6 s the left hand opened and moved away, and all five cards fell onto the table; both arms then rose and stayed raised for the rest of the 1,000 steps); demo: 1.0 (the trial ended with full score at step 470 of 1,000)
